reviews.summary: This paper examines whether gravitational-wave signals from eccentric EMRIs can distinguish dark-matter halos from accretion disks. It combines numerical-kludge waveforms with NFW and Beta halo profiles and a thin alpha-disk prescription, comparing phase responses, one-radian distinguishability times and noise-weighted LISA residuals. In the benchmark systems, disk-induced dephasing changes more strongly with initial eccentricity than halo-induced dephasing. However, observation duration and environmental strength dominate detectability; eccentricity provides an auxiliary diagnostic. The contribution is a direct comparison of two environmental interpretations using complementary phase and detector-weighted measures. The reported residuals exceed unity for the chosen configurations, but these comparisons should not be read as a demonstration that the environments remain distinguishable after fitting all source parameters.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly connects EMRIs, gravitational waves and environmental effects, with eccentricity-dependent waveform diagnostics for LISA.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text defines explicit diagnostics and evaluates several environmental strengths and observation durations. Its support is conditional on approximate waveforms and fixed benchmark comparisons rather than a complete inference study.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, opening of Sec. II, portions of Sec. IV, Sec. V and part of Appendix A. Benchmarks restrict initial eccentricity to 0–0.1 and use a spherical background. The inspected residual calculation does not establish distinguishability after full parameter fitting. Figures were not visually inspected; derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: the dominant factor controlling the distinguishability between the two waveforms is still the observation duration.

reviews.summary: This study investigates how rotation changes scalar-wave transmission through a traversable wormhole of the Teo class. The authors solve the scattering problem, compute transmission probabilities and extract long-lived quasinormal frequencies by direct integration. Rotation deepens the trapping cavity for counter-rotating modes, producing narrow transmission resonances associated with weakly damped modes. Corotating modes instead develop an ergoregion instability, so the reported cross-section comparisons focus on stable partial waves. Frequency-refinement checks and a conserved-flux diagnostic support the numerical calculations. The contribution is a connection between rotational trapping, resonant transmission and mode stability in a concrete horizonless geometry. Its implications for gravitational-wave observations remain prospective because the calculations concern a test scalar field rather than gravitational perturbations.
reviews.relevance_reason: Relevant to resonances, quasinormal modes and compact-object perturbations, but it treats an exotic wormhole and scalar scattering rather than astrophysical black-hole waveforms.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text connects resonances to independently computed complex frequencies and reports frequency refinement, flux conservation and recovery of static scattering results. These provide substantial internal numerical checks within the chosen model.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, part of Sec. 1, numerical checks in Sec. 4.1, portions of Sec. 4.2 and Sec. 7. Only one Teo-class geometry and a massless scalar are studied; stable partial-wave results do not resolve the unstable background's full physical interpretation. Figures were not visually inspected; derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_location: Sec. 4.1, Numerical validation of the flux conservation
reviews.evidence_quote: we verify the conservation of the scalar field flux

reviews.summary: This paper studies how uncertain Delta-baryon interactions affect inspiral signals from hyperonic neutron stars. It constructs density-dependent relativistic mean-field equations of state, solves stellar-structure and tidal-response equations, then inserts the resulting deformabilities into TaylorT4 inspiral waveforms. Varying the selected meson couplings changes stellar compactness and late-inspiral phase evolution. For the compared models, aligned phase differences reach roughly 2.5–3.4 radians at 1400 Hz. Noise-weighted mismatches suggest characteristic signal-to-noise ratios around 8–11 within the restricted analysis band. The contribution is a quantified link between a dense-matter coupling choice and waveform differences. The authors explicitly caution that these are not unique Delta-baryon signatures: different compositions with the same relevant tidal properties can produce indistinguishable signals.
reviews.relevance_reason: Useful for gravitational-wave inspirals and tidal deformability. Here 'Delta resonances' denotes baryonic degrees of freedom, not the orbital or tidal resonance dynamics central to several selected interests.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text connects EOS calculations to aligned waveforms and detector-weighted mismatches, with explicit degeneracy caveats. The evidence remains model-dependent and does not establish composition inference with freely fitted masses and spins.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, parts of the Introduction, TaylorT4 caveat, mismatch discussion and Sec. IV. Fixed dense-matter framework, equal-mass binaries and perturbative late-inspiral waveforms limit generalization; band-limited SNR estimates are not detection or composition-identification thresholds. Figures were not visually inspected; derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: these are preliminary waveform-separation estimates rather than composition-identification thresholds.

reviews.summary: This work addresses why quasinormal modes alone cannot represent a black hole's response at every time. It splits the frequency-domain Green function into pieces whose integration contours depend on spacetime region. Late-time responses admit quasinormal-mode sums, while earlier responses require Matsubara-mode sums associated with the Euclidean thermal circle. The authors analyze Pöschl–Teller, BTZ and Schwarzschild examples, using residue asymptotics and convergence tests, alongside numerical partial-sum comparisons. For Schwarzschild, a small positive cosmological constant resolves the branch cut into poles and recovers the tail through a limiting construction. The contribution is a broader framework for mode completeness and ringdown interpretation, with implications for fitting generic initial data. The demonstrated setting is static, so application to Kerr remains an extension.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly central to quasinormal modes, black-hole perturbation theory, Green functions and the interpretation of gravitational-wave ringdown.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected analysis presents explicit residue convergence tests and numerical Green-function comparisons across several models. It also distinguishes the limiting treatment of Schwarzschild tails from a naive pure-QNM expansion.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, portions of Sec. II.1, Sec. IV.2–IV.4 and Sec. VI. The detailed proofs and all appendices were not checked. Static backgrounds and fixed angular harmonics limit direct use for Kerr or full waveforms. Figures were not visually inspected; derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: we perform partial sums and compare to a numerical solution

reviews.summary: This paper develops a time-domain calculation of gravitational-wave lensing by a Kerr black hole. A localized hyperboloidal slicing and static field redefinition stabilize explicit evolution, while tetrad projections and angular rotations accommodate arbitrary incident directions and polarizations. The numerical examples evolve more than 68,000 coupled angular modes. Wave packets form a forward, approximately Gaussian beam: the prompt response is nearly spin-insensitive, whereas the later coda depends on rotation. In the studied binary-coalescence examples, Kerr and Schwarzschild lensed waveforms have extremely small reported mismatches. The contribution combines a substantial computational framework with a possible shortcut for lensing searches. That shortcut should be interpreted within the simulated geometry and parameter choices, rather than as a general result for every lensing configuration.
reviews.relevance_reason: Direct intersection of gravitational lensing, gravitational waves, Teukolsky evolution and black-hole perturbation theory.
reviews.quality_reason: The text specifies a detailed numerical formulation and compares inclination and polarization cases. The very small reported mismatches and broad surrogate claim require numerical-error and parameter-domain assessment beyond what this selective reading establishes.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, numerical setup and portions of Sec. VII, and Sec. VIII. Binary examples use a particular source, lens mass, spin and on-axis downstream observer; these do not establish general spin insensitivity. Resolution errors at the quoted mismatch scale were not assessed here. Figures were not visually inspected; derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_location: Sec. VII, Numerical Results; benchmark spin a/M=0.7
reviews.evidence_quote: we fix the dimensionless spin parameter at

reviews.summary: This paper revisits puzzling Kerr quasinormal modes near algebraically special frequencies, where numerical branches appear to split or disappear. It tracks both poles and Matsubara-frequency zeros of Green-function building blocks across conventional and unconventional Riemann sheets. The apparent bifurcation becomes an avoided crossing with a neighboring mode, accompanied by enhanced excitation factors. Apparent disappearance instead follows a pole-zero cancellation in the reciprocal incident amplitude. Examples for several gravitational multipoles support a common mechanism, and an analytic frequency relation explains the nonrotating cancellation. The contribution is a unified interpretation of anomalous spectral behavior using poles, zeros and residues together. Observable waveform consequences still require the source-dependent excitation and the precise Green-function criterion to be specified.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly addresses Kerr quasinormal modes, resonant excitation, Teukolsky scattering and black-hole perturbation theory.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text combines pole trajectories, excitation residues, an explicit zero-frequency relation and examples beyond a single multipole. It carefully qualifies the meaning of disappearance by the incident-amplitude criterion.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, substantial portions of the avoided-crossing and pole-skipping analyses, and Conclusions and Discussion. Supplemental derivations were not checked. Large excitation factors alone do not determine a measurable signal because source weights also enter. Figures were not visually inspected; derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: the corresponding QNM pole is canceled by the Matsubara zero in the reciprocal incident amplitude.

reviews.summary: This study separates quasinormal spectral sensitivity, exponential instability and superradiant amplification for charged scalar fields around charged black holes. It adds a localized positive potential bump and compares mode migration with real-frequency scattering on Reissner–Nordström and de Sitter backgrounds. Shooting, spectral collocation and selected growing-root counts provide complementary numerical diagnostics. In the asymptotically flat examples, damped modes can enter the superradiant frequency range without creating narrow amplification peaks. In selected de Sitter cases, the bump removes a growing monopole even while substantial amplification persists. The contribution is a clear counterexample to treating these three phenomena as equivalent. The stabilization claim applies to sampled configurations of a prescribed scalar potential, not to a general self-consistent astrophysical environment.
reviews.relevance_reason: Strong overlap with quasinormal modes, environmental perturbations and resonant scattering, although the charged test-scalar backgrounds are idealized.
reviews.quality_reason: The paper reports independent numerical methods, flux tests and bounded growing-root searches. Its own appendix notes missing contour-resolution diagnostics, limiting how strongly the selected stability counts can be independently assessed.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, Sec. IV and opening of V, portions of VI, Sec. VII and Appendix C.2. Only monopoles and specified bump profiles are tested; cutoff sensitivity and full contour diagnostics remain limitations. These are not gravitational-wave predictions or a nonlinear stability proof. Figures were not visually inspected; derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: They are numerical counts, not interval-arithmetic proofs.

reviews.summary: SPLIT addresses biases that arise when long EMRI or IMRI signals are analyzed with imperfect, fully coherent waveform models. It divides data into shorter coherent blocks and couples their evolving parameters through a flexible Markovian Student-t prior, with a heavy-tailed likelihood for robustness. A GPU implementation uses sequential Gibbs sampling to explore the enlarged posterior. Vacuum-signal tests agree with coherent baselines, while an accretion-perturbed IMRI example reduces the largest reported one-dimensional bias from about 4.8 to 0.5 standard deviations. The contribution is a practical intermediate inference framework between independent segments and strict coherence. This improvement trades away precision and computational efficiency; it is not a replacement for accurately modeled coherent inference or a demonstrated solution to every realistic LISA noise artifact.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly useful for EMRI/IMRI gravitational-wave inference and robustness against unmodeled environmental effects.
reviews.quality_reason: The inspected text provides a defined statistical model, coherent control cases, a misspecified environmental injection and explicit cost and bias comparisons. It acknowledges the precision trade-off and need for broader hyperparameter studies.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, portions of Sec. III.4 and Sec. IV. The environmental example fixes primary spin to zero and studies a limited injection set. Hyperparameters affect results; five-block sampling took about 3.4 days versus roughly five hours for the coherent case. Figures were not visually inspected; code was not run and derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: the chain convergence rate is still significantly slower than in the fully-coherent case.

reviews.summary: This paper examines when bound-state spectra can be analytically continued into black-hole quasinormal frequencies. Using perturbed delta-function and Pöschl–Teller potentials, it separates continuation of an exact spectral equation from continuation of a truncated perturbative answer. Small deformations near the barrier maximum can yield useful mapped frequencies. For distant deformations, however, a controlled first-order bound-state correction can become greatly amplified after continuation and disagree with directly computed quasinormal modes. Matrix-method comparisons illustrate the failure at higher overtones. The contribution is a concrete warning that well-behaved bound-state perturbation theory does not automatically control the corresponding open-system spectrum. The results constrain the tested approximation; they do not establish that every analytic-continuation approach fails or identify an exact convergence singularity.
reviews.relevance_reason: Central to quasinormal-mode calculations, black-hole perturbation theory and spectral sensitivity to environmental potential changes.
reviews.quality_reason: Analytically tractable models and direct numerical comparisons support the caution about first-order mappings. The paper explicitly separates approximation failure from an unproven breakdown of the exact continuation.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, parts of the Introduction, Secs. VI–VII, opening of Appendix A and incidental portions of Appendix C. Full proofs were not checked. Results concern simplified potentials and first-order corrections; higher-order error estimates and a convergence-limiting singularity are not established. Figures were not visually inspected; derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_location: Sec. VI, Numerical results and comparison with other approaches
reviews.evidence_quote: The calculation does not provide higher-order error estimates

reviews.summary: This paper presents a cheaper way to include leading resistive effects in general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamics. Its REGIME formulation expands around the ideal-MHD limit using fluid-frame variables, avoiding matrix inversions and implicit time integration. Implemented in IllinoisGRMHD, it is tested against current-sheet diffusion and magnetized stellar evolutions before application to an equal-mass neutron-star merger. The examples show resistive magnetic dissipation, altered remnant structure and differences in post-merger gravitational-wave phase and amplitude. The measured computational overhead relative to ideal MHD is modest. The contribution is a practical high-conductivity approximation for existing simulation infrastructure. Merger results remain proof of principle: binary grid convergence is deferred, and stronger claims about angular-momentum transport or observable waveform changes require further analysis.
reviews.relevance_reason: Directly central to GRMHD, relativistic hydrodynamics and gravitational-wave predictions from neutron-star mergers.
reviews.quality_reason: Analytic diffusion comparisons and reported second-order tests support the numerical method. Physical conclusions from the binary example remain preliminary because merger convergence and a dedicated transport analysis are deferred.
reviews.limitations: Selective reading: abstract, Introduction, current-sheet tests in Sec. IV.1, portions of Sec. V.1–V.2 and Sec. VI. The method is a leading high-conductivity expansion; binary convergence is deferred, the atmosphere is nearly ideal rather than electrovacuum, and the example uses a strong initial magnetic field. Figures were not visually inspected; simulations were not run and derivations were not independently verified.
reviews.evidence_quote: The simple discretisations performed in this proof-of-principle paper therefore have limited, second-order, numerical accuracy.
